# noxu_persist - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/noxu-persist/^7.2.1/

## Expand description

Internal component of the[database.](https://crates.io/crates/noxu)`noxu`This crate is published only so the

`noxu`umbrella crate can depend on it. Use`noxu`(`noxu = "7"`) in applications; depend on this crate directly only if you are extending the engine internals. Its API may change without a major version bump.

Note on derive macros:`#[derive(Entity)]`,`#[derive(PrimaryKey)]`, and`#[derive(SecondaryKey)]`emit`::noxu::persist::`paths in generated code by default, so the`noxu`umbrella crate must be present. Users who depend on`noxu-persist`directly (without the umbrella) can add`#[entity(crate = "noxu_persist")]`to each struct to redirect generated code to`::noxu_persist::…`instead — see the[crate-path escape hatch](https://docs.rs#crate-path-escape-hatch)section below.

Derive-macro-based entity persistence for Noxu DB.

Direct Persistence Layer — provides trait-based entity-to-database mapping with a proc-macro derive shortcut.

[§](https://docs.rs#umbrella-usage-recommended)Umbrella usage (recommended)

Most users depend on the `noxu` umbrella crate and use `noxu::persist`
as their import path.  The derive macros default to emitting
`::noxu::persist::…` paths, which works automatically:

```
use noxu::persist::{Entity, SecondaryKey};
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Entity, SecondaryKey)]
struct User {
    #[primary_key]
    id: u64,
    #[secondary_key(name = "by_email", relate = OneToOne)]
    email: String,
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#crate-path-escape-hatch)Crate-path escape hatch

Users who add `noxu-persist` as a **direct** dependency (without the
`noxu` umbrella) can add `#[entity(crate = "noxu_persist")]` to each
annotated struct.  Generated code then uses `::noxu_persist::…` paths
instead, and the umbrella crate is not required.

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
// Cargo.toml: noxu-persist = "3"  (no noxu umbrella)
use noxu_persist::{Entity, SecondaryKey};
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Entity, SecondaryKey)]
#[entity(crate = "noxu_persist")]
struct Widget {
    #[primary_key]
    id: u64,
    #[secondary_key(name = "by_kind", relate = ManyToOne)]
    kind: String,
}
```
The same `#[entity(crate = "…")]` attribute is recognised by all three
derives: `Entity`, `PrimaryKey`, and `SecondaryKey`.  Any valid Rust
module path is accepted; a malformed path produces a descriptive
compile error.

[§](https://docs.rs#overview)Overview

The persistence layer provides typed access to database records through:

- `Entity`
- `PrimaryKey`
- `EntitySerializer`
- `PrimaryIndex`
- `EntityStore`
- `StoreConfig`

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
use noxu_persist::*;
use noxu_db::{Environment, EnvironmentConfig};
// Define an entity
struct User { id: u64, name: String }
impl Entity for User {
    type PrimaryKey = u64;
    fn primary_key(&self) -> &u64 { &self.id }
    fn entity_name() -> &'static str { "User" }
}
// Define a serializer
struct UserSerializer;
impl EntitySerializer<User> for UserSerializer {
    fn serialize(&self, user: &User) -> error::Result<Vec<u8>> { /* ... */ }
    fn deserialize(&self, bytes: &[u8]) -> error::Result<User> { /* ... */ }
}
// Use the store
let config = StoreConfig::new("my_store").with_allow_create(true);
// let mut store = EntityStore::open(&env, config)?;
// let index: PrimaryIndex<u64, User> = store.get_primary_index()?;
// index.put(&UserSerializer, &User { id: 1, name: "Alice".into() })?;
```

# noxu_persist_derive - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/noxu-persist-derive/^7.2.1/

## Expand description

Internal component of the[database.](https://crates.io/crates/noxu)`noxu`This crate is published only so the

`noxu`umbrella crate can depend on it. Use`noxu`(`noxu = "7"`) in applications; depend on this crate directly only if you are extending the engine internals. Its API may change without a major version bump.

Derive macros for the Noxu DB Direct Persistence Layer (DPL).

This crate provides three `#[derive(...)]` macros that generate the
boilerplate required to use a Rust struct with `noxu-persist`:

-
`#[derive(Entity)]``noxu_persist::Entity`for a user struct. The struct must have exactly one field annotated with`#[primary_key]`; the field’s type becomes`Entity::PrimaryKey`. By default the entity name is the struct name; override with`#[entity(name = "...")]`at the struct level.
-
`#[derive(PrimaryKey)]``noxu_persist::PrimaryKey`for a user struct used as a*composite*or*newtype*primary key (analogue of`@KeyField`from BDB-JE). Supports tuple structs with one field (newtype) and named-field structs (composite, length-prefix concatenation). The struct must also derive`Clone + PartialEq + Eq + Hash`for the`PrimaryKey`trait bounds; this is the user’s responsibility.
-
`#[derive(SecondaryKey)]``#[secondary_key(...)]`field on the user struct, emits a typed`Foo::open_<name>_index(primary)`helper method that opens a`noxu_persist::SecondaryIndex`against a`PrimaryIndex`, plus a`pub const SECONDARY_INDEXES: &'static [SecondarySpec]`table describing every declared index. This derive is independent of`derive(Entity)`(you can use either or both).

[§](https://docs.rs#why-three-macros)Why three macros?

BDB-JE has three annotations: `@Entity`, `@PrimaryKey`,
`@SecondaryKey` — each addressing a different concern.  The Noxu
port preserves the same factoring so the porting guidance is
mechanical:

| JE annotation | Noxu derive |
|---|---|
| `@Entity` | `#[derive(Entity)]`(struct level) |
| `@PrimaryKey`(field) | `#[primary_key]`(consumed by`Entity`derive) |
| `@PrimaryKeyField`/`@KeyField` | `#[derive(PrimaryKey)]`(struct level for composite key types) |
| `@SecondaryKey(name=…, relate=…, …)` | `#[secondary_key(name=…, relate=…, …)]`(field level, consumed by`SecondaryKey`derive) |

[§](https://docs.rs#crate-path-escape-hatch)Crate-path escape hatch

By default the generated code emits `::noxu::persist::…` paths, so
the `noxu` umbrella crate must be in the dependency graph.  Users who
depend on `noxu-persist` **directly** (without the umbrella) can
override this with the `crate` key inside the `#[entity(…)]`
container attribute:

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
// Cargo.toml: noxu-persist = "3"  (no noxu umbrella needed)
use noxu_persist::{Entity, PrimaryKey, SecondaryKey};
#[derive(Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, PrimaryKey)]
#[entity(crate = "noxu_persist")]
struct UserId(u64);
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Entity, SecondaryKey)]
#[entity(crate = "noxu_persist")]
struct User {
    #[primary_key]
    id: UserId,
    #[secondary_key(name = "by_email", relate = OneToOne)]
    email: String,
}
```
The `crate` key is accepted by all three derives via the
`#[entity(crate = "…")]` form.  A string literal containing a valid
Rust module path is required (validated at compile time); a malformed
path produces a descriptive compile error.

[§](https://docs.rs#re-exports)Re-exports

The `noxu-persist` crate re-exports all three derives so users only
need a single dependency:

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
use noxu_persist::{Entity, PrimaryKey, SecondaryKey};
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Entity, SecondaryKey)]
#[entity(crate = "noxu_persist")]
struct User {
    #[primary_key]
    id: u64,
    #[secondary_key(name = "by_email", relate = OneToOne)]
    email: String,
    #[secondary_key(name = "by_dept", relate = ManyToOne, related_entity = "Department")]
    dept: Option<u64>,
}
```
## Derive Macros[§](https://docs.rs#derives)

- [Entity](https://docs.rs/derive.Entity.html)
- Derive `noxu_persist::Entity`for a struct.
- [Primary](https://docs.rs/derive.PrimaryKey.html)- Key
- Derive `noxu_persist::PrimaryKey`for a custom key struct.
- [Secondary](https://docs.rs/derive.SecondaryKey.html)- Key
- Derive secondary-index helpers for fields annotated with
`#[secondary_key(...)]`.

# noxu_rep - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/noxu-rep/^7.2.1/

## Expand description

Internal component of the[database.](https://crates.io/crates/noxu)`noxu`This crate is published only so the

`noxu`umbrella crate can depend on it. Use`noxu`(`noxu = "7"`) in applications; depend on this crate directly only if you are extending the engine internals. Its API may change without a major version bump.

Replication and high availability for Noxu DB.

master-replica replication with automatic elections, VLSN tracking, network restore, and subscription.

[§](https://docs.rs#architecture)Architecture

The replication layer consists of:

- **ReplicatedEnvironment**– Entry point that wraps a standard Environment and adds replication capabilities. Rep.ReplicatedEnvironment`.
- **Elections**– Automatic master election using majority voting. Rep.elections`.
- **VLSN Index**– Maps version sequence numbers to log file positions.
- **Feeder/Replica Stream**– Master-to-replica log entry streaming. Port
- **Network Transport**– Pluggable channel-based communication. Rep.net`.
- **Group Service**– Replication group membership management.
- **Consistency Policies**– Configurable replica consistency guarantees.
- **Master Transfer**– Controlled transfer of master role.
- **Network Restore**– Full node restore from another replica.
- **Subscription**– External subscription to the replication stream.

[§](https://docs.rs#node-states)Node States

A replication node transitions through the following states:

- **Detached**– Not associated with the group (handle closed).
- **Unknown**– Not in contact with the master, actively trying to establish contact or decide upon a master.
- **Master**– The unique master of the group; can read and write.
- **Replica**– Being updated by the master; read-only.

The state transitions visible to the application follow:

`[ MASTER | REPLICA | UNKNOWN ]+ DETACHED`[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
use noxu_rep::{ReplicatedEnvironment, RepConfig, NodeType};
let config = RepConfig::builder("my_group", "node1", "localhost")
    .node_port(14_001)
    .node_type(NodeType::Electable)
    .build();
let rep_env = ReplicatedEnvironment::new(config).unwrap();
```

# noxu_xa - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/noxu-xa/^7.2.1/

## Expand description

Internal component of the[database.](https://crates.io/crates/noxu)`noxu`This crate is published only so the

`noxu`umbrella crate can depend on it. Use`noxu`(`noxu = "7"`) in applications; depend on this crate directly only if you are extending the engine internals. Its API may change without a major version bump.

XA distributed transaction support for Noxu DB.

This crate implements the X/Open XA interface for coordinating distributed transactions across multiple Noxu environments. It provides:

- `Xid`— XA transaction identifier (format_id + global_transaction_id + branch_qualifier)
- `XaFlags`— flags for XA operations (JOIN, RESUME, TMSUCCESS, ONEPHASE, etc.)
- `XaResource`— trait defining the XA resource manager interface
- `XaEnvironment`— implementation of- `XaResource`backed by a Noxu Environment

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
use noxu_xa::{XaEnvironment, XaResource, Xid, XaFlags, PrepareResult};
let xa = XaEnvironment::new(env);
let xid = Xid::new(1, b"global_txn_1", b"branch_1").unwrap();
xa.xa_start(&xid, XaFlags::NOFLAGS)?;
// ... perform database operations using xa.get_transaction(&xid) ...
xa.xa_end(&xid, XaFlags::TMSUCCESS)?;
match xa.xa_prepare(&xid, XaFlags::NOFLAGS)? {
    PrepareResult::Ok => xa.xa_commit(&xid, XaFlags::NOFLAGS)?,
    PrepareResult::ReadOnly => {} // no commit needed
}
```

# noxu - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/noxu/7.2.1/target-redirect/noxu/

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#noxu-db--umbrella-crate)Noxu DB — umbrella crate

** noxu** is the single crate users depend on to get the full
Noxu DB engine.  It re-exports the public API of all component crates
behind a single name and version so you write only:

```
[dependencies]
noxu = "7"
```
[§](https://docs.rs#quick-start)Quick-start

```
use noxu::{DatabaseConfig, Environment, EnvironmentConfig};
use std::path::PathBuf;
let env = Environment::open(
    EnvironmentConfig::new(PathBuf::from("/tmp/mydb"))
        .with_allow_create(true)
        .with_transactional(true),
)?;
let db_config = DatabaseConfig::new()
    .with_allow_create(true)
    .with_transactional(true);
let db = env.open_database(None, "kv", &db_config)?;
let txn = env.begin_transaction(None)?;
db.put_in(&txn, b"hello", b"world")?;
txn.commit()?;
// Reads return `Result<Option<Bytes>>`.
if let Some(value) = db.get(b"hello")? {
    assert_eq!(value.as_ref(), b"world");
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#feature-flags)Feature flags

| Feature | Default | What it enables |
|---|---|---|
| `collections` | yes | module —`collections``StoredMap`,`StoredSet`,`StoredList` |
| `persist` | yes | module —`persist``#[derive(Entity)]`,`PrimaryIndex`,`EntityStore` |
| `xa` | yes | module — XA two-phase-commit (`xa``XaEnvironment`) |
| `replication` | no | `replication`module — master-replica HA, elections |
| `replication-tls-rustls` | no | TLS for replication via pure-Rust `rustls` |
| `replication-tls-native` | no | TLS for replication via OS/OpenSSL |
| `observability` | no | `observe`module —`tracing`+`metrics`glue |

[§](https://docs.rs#using-noxu-from-async-code)Using Noxu from async code

**Noxu is synchronous by design.** Every operation (`get`, `put`,
`commit`, cursor navigation, `Environment::open`) is blocking: it does
real disk I/O, acquires locks, and may park the calling thread. There is
no `async` API and none is planned — the engine uses explicit threads and
blocking I/O throughout (only the optional `replication` feature’s
networking uses `tokio` internally).

If you call Noxu from inside a `tokio` (or other async) runtime, do **not**
call it directly on an async worker thread — a blocking call there stalls
every other task sharing that worker. Instead, move the work onto a
blocking thread:

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
// `env` is Send + Sync; clone the Arc into the blocking task.
let value = tokio::task::spawn_blocking(move || {
    let db_cfg = noxu::DatabaseConfig::new().with_allow_create(true);
    let db = env.open_database(None, "users", &db_cfg)?;
    db.put(b"k", b"v")?;
    db.get(b"k")
})
.await??; // first `?`: JoinError; second `?`: NoxuError
```
Guidelines:

- Wrap each unit of Noxu work in `tokio::task::spawn_blocking`(or a dedicated blocking thread pool), not the async path.
- **Never hold a**A transaction holds locks; suspending the task while it is open can block other writers indefinitely and the borrow on the transaction would also prevent the future from being- `Transaction`- `Cursor`- `.await`.- `Send`. Open, use, and commit/abort a transaction entirely within one- `spawn_blocking`closure.
- `Environment`is- `Send + Sync`, so share it across tasks via- `Arc<Environment>`and open per-task databases/transactions inside the blocking closure.

[§](https://docs.rs#derive-macros)Derive macros

With the `persist` feature (on by default) the derive macros
`Entity`, `PrimaryKey`, and `SecondaryKey` are available directly
through this crate:

```
use noxu::persist::{Entity, SecondaryKey};
#[derive(Clone, Entity, SecondaryKey)]
struct User {
    #[primary_key]
    id: u64,
    #[secondary_key(name = "by_email", relate = OneToOne)]
    email: String,
}
```

# noxu/lib.rs

[1](https://docs.rs#1)// Copyright (C) 2024-2025 Greg Burd.  Licensed under either of the
[2](https://docs.rs#2)// Apache License, Version 2.0 or the MIT license, at your option.
[3](https://docs.rs#3)// See LICENSE-APACHE and LICENSE-MIT at the root of this repository.
[4](https://docs.rs#4)// SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0 OR MIT
[5](https://docs.rs#5)
[6](https://docs.rs#6)//! # Noxu DB — umbrella crate
[7](https://docs.rs#7)//!
[8](https://docs.rs#8)//! **`noxu`** is the single crate users depend on to get the full
[9](https://docs.rs#9)//! Noxu DB engine.  It re-exports the public API of all component crates
[10](https://docs.rs#10)//! behind a single name and version so you write only:
[11](https://docs.rs#11)//!
[12](https://docs.rs#12)//! ```toml
[13](https://docs.rs#13)//! [dependencies]
[14](https://docs.rs#14)//! noxu = "7"
[15](https://docs.rs#15)//! ```
[16](https://docs.rs#16)//!
[17](https://docs.rs#17)//! ## Quick-start
[18](https://docs.rs#18)//!
[19](https://docs.rs#19)//! ```no_run
[20](https://docs.rs#20)//! use noxu::{DatabaseConfig, Environment, EnvironmentConfig};
[21](https://docs.rs#21)//! use std::path::PathBuf;
[22](https://docs.rs#22)//!
[23](https://docs.rs#23)//! # fn main() -> noxu::Result<()> {
[24](https://docs.rs#24)//! let env = Environment::open(
[25](https://docs.rs#25)//!     EnvironmentConfig::new(PathBuf::from("/tmp/mydb"))
[26](https://docs.rs#26)//!         .with_allow_create(true)
[27](https://docs.rs#27)//!         .with_transactional(true),
[28](https://docs.rs#28)//! )?;
[29](https://docs.rs#29)//! let db_config = DatabaseConfig::new()
[30](https://docs.rs#30)//!     .with_allow_create(true)
[31](https://docs.rs#31)//!     .with_transactional(true);
[32](https://docs.rs#32)//! let db = env.open_database(None, "kv", &db_config)?;
[33](https://docs.rs#33)//! let txn = env.begin_transaction(None)?;
[34](https://docs.rs#34)//! db.put_in(&txn, b"hello", b"world")?;
[35](https://docs.rs#35)//! txn.commit()?;
[36](https://docs.rs#36)//!
[37](https://docs.rs#37)//! // Reads return `Result<Option<Bytes>>`.
[38](https://docs.rs#38)//! if let Some(value) = db.get(b"hello")? {
[39](https://docs.rs#39)//!     assert_eq!(value.as_ref(), b"world");
[40](https://docs.rs#40)//! }
[41](https://docs.rs#41)//! # Ok(())
[42](https://docs.rs#42)//! # }
[43](https://docs.rs#43)//! ```
[44](https://docs.rs#44)//!
[45](https://docs.rs#45)//! ## Feature flags
[46](https://docs.rs#46)//!
[47](https://docs.rs#47)//! | Feature | Default | What it enables |
[48](https://docs.rs#48)//! |---|---|---|
[49](https://docs.rs#49)//! | `collections` | yes | [`collections`] module — `StoredMap`, `StoredSet`, `StoredList` |
[50](https://docs.rs#50)//! | `persist` | yes | [`persist`] module — `#[derive(Entity)]`, `PrimaryIndex`, `EntityStore` |
[51](https://docs.rs#51)//! | `xa` | yes | [`xa`] module — XA two-phase-commit (`XaEnvironment`) |
[52](https://docs.rs#52)//! | `replication` | no | `replication` module — master-replica HA, elections |
[53](https://docs.rs#53)//! | `replication-tls-rustls` | no | TLS for replication via pure-Rust `rustls` |
[54](https://docs.rs#54)//! | `replication-tls-native` | no | TLS for replication via OS/OpenSSL |
[55](https://docs.rs#55)//! | `observability` | no | `observe` module — `tracing` + `metrics` glue |
[56](https://docs.rs#56)//!
[57](https://docs.rs#57)//! ## Using Noxu from async code
[58](https://docs.rs#58)//!
[59](https://docs.rs#59)//! **Noxu is synchronous by design.** Every operation (`get`, `put`,
[60](https://docs.rs#60)//! `commit`, cursor navigation, `Environment::open`) is blocking: it does
[61](https://docs.rs#61)//! real disk I/O, acquires locks, and may park the calling thread. There is
[62](https://docs.rs#62)//! no `async` API and none is planned — the engine uses explicit threads and
[63](https://docs.rs#63)//! blocking I/O throughout (only the optional `replication` feature's
[64](https://docs.rs#64)//! networking uses `tokio` internally).
[65](https://docs.rs#65)//!
[66](https://docs.rs#66)//! If you call Noxu from inside a `tokio` (or other async) runtime, do **not**
[67](https://docs.rs#67)//! call it directly on an async worker thread — a blocking call there stalls
[68](https://docs.rs#68)//! every other task sharing that worker. Instead, move the work onto a
[69](https://docs.rs#69)//! blocking thread:
[70](https://docs.rs#70)//!
[71](https://docs.rs#71)//! ```ignore
[72](https://docs.rs#72)//! # async fn example(env: std::sync::Arc<noxu::Environment>) -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
[73](https://docs.rs#73)//! // `env` is Send + Sync; clone the Arc into the blocking task.
[74](https://docs.rs#74)//! let value = tokio::task::spawn_blocking(move || {
[75](https://docs.rs#75)//!     let db_cfg = noxu::DatabaseConfig::new().with_allow_create(true);
[76](https://docs.rs#76)//!     let db = env.open_database(None, "users", &db_cfg)?;
[77](https://docs.rs#77)//!     db.put(b"k", b"v")?;
[78](https://docs.rs#78)//!     db.get(b"k")
[79](https://docs.rs#79)//! })
[80](https://docs.rs#80)//! .await??; // first `?`: JoinError; second `?`: NoxuError
[81](https://docs.rs#81)//! # let _ = value;
[82](https://docs.rs#82)//! # Ok(())
[83](https://docs.rs#83)//! # }
[84](https://docs.rs#84)//! ```
[85](https://docs.rs#85)//!
[86](https://docs.rs#86)//! Guidelines:
[87](https://docs.rs#87)//!
[88](https://docs.rs#88)//! - Wrap each unit of Noxu work in `tokio::task::spawn_blocking` (or a
[89](https://docs.rs#89)//!   dedicated blocking thread pool), not the async path.
[90](https://docs.rs#90)//! - **Never hold a [`Transaction`] (or an open [`Cursor`]) across an
[91](https://docs.rs#91)//!   `.await`.** A transaction holds locks; suspending the task while it is
[92](https://docs.rs#92)//!   open can block other writers indefinitely and the borrow on the
[93](https://docs.rs#93)//!   transaction would also prevent the future from being `Send`. Open,
[94](https://docs.rs#94)//!   use, and commit/abort a transaction entirely within one
[95](https://docs.rs#95)//!   `spawn_blocking` closure.
[96](https://docs.rs#96)//! - `Environment` is `Send + Sync`, so share it across tasks via
[97](https://docs.rs#97)//!   `Arc<Environment>` and open per-task databases/transactions inside the
[98](https://docs.rs#98)//!   blocking closure.
[99](https://docs.rs#99)//!
[100](https://docs.rs#100)//! ## Derive macros
[101](https://docs.rs#101)//!
[102](https://docs.rs#102)//! With the `persist` feature (on by default) the derive macros
[103](https://docs.rs#103)//! `Entity`, `PrimaryKey`, and `SecondaryKey` are available directly
[104](https://docs.rs#104)//! through this crate:
[105](https://docs.rs#105)//!
[106](https://docs.rs#106)//! ```no_run
[107](https://docs.rs#107)//! use noxu::persist::{Entity, SecondaryKey};
[108](https://docs.rs#108)//!
[109](https://docs.rs#109)//! #[derive(Clone, Entity, SecondaryKey)]
[110](https://docs.rs#110)//! struct User {
[111](https://docs.rs#111)//!     #[primary_key]
[112](https://docs.rs#112)//!     id: u64,
[113](https://docs.rs#113)//!     #[secondary_key(name = "by_email", relate = OneToOne)]
[114](https://docs.rs#114)//!     email: String,
[115](https://docs.rs#115)//! }
[116](https://docs.rs#116)//! ```
[117](https://docs.rs#117)
[118](https://docs.rs#118)// Re-export the entire core public API at the crate root.
[119](https://docs.rs#119)pub use noxu_db::*;
[120](https://docs.rs#120)
[121](https://docs.rs#121)/// Binding helpers: tuple encoding, entry views, serial encoding.
[122](https://docs.rs#122)pub mod bind {
[123](https://docs.rs#123)    pub use noxu_bind::*;
[124](https://docs.rs#124)}
[125](https://docs.rs#125)
[126](https://docs.rs#126)/// Iterator-based collection views (`StoredMap`, `StoredSet`, `StoredList`).
[127](https://docs.rs#127)#[cfg(feature = "collections")]
[128](https://docs.rs#128)pub mod collections {
[129](https://docs.rs#129)    pub use noxu_collections::*;
[130](https://docs.rs#130)}
[131](https://docs.rs#131)
[132](https://docs.rs#132)/// Trait-based entity persistence (DPL): `Entity`, `PrimaryKey`,
[133](https://docs.rs#133)/// `PrimaryIndex`, `EntityStore`, and the derive macros.
[134](https://docs.rs#134)///
[135](https://docs.rs#135)/// The derive macros (`#[derive(Entity)]`, `#[derive(PrimaryKey)]`,
[136](https://docs.rs#136)/// `#[derive(SecondaryKey)]`) are re-exported here so that the generated
[137](https://docs.rs#137)/// code — which references `::noxu::persist::…` paths — resolves
[138](https://docs.rs#138)/// correctly when the user only depends on the `noxu` umbrella crate.
[139](https://docs.rs#139)#[cfg(feature = "persist")]

# noxu::persist - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/noxu/7.2.1/noxu/persist/index.html

## Expand description

Trait-based entity persistence (DPL): `Entity`, `PrimaryKey`,
`PrimaryIndex`, `EntityStore`, and the derive macros.

The derive macros (`#[derive(Entity)]`, `#[derive(PrimaryKey)]`,
`#[derive(SecondaryKey)]`) are re-exported here so that the generated
code — which references `::noxu::persist::…` paths — resolves
correctly when the user only depends on the `noxu` umbrella crate.

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [entity](https://docs.rs/entity/index.html)
- Entity and key traits for the persistence layer.
- [entity_](https://docs.rs/entity_serializer/index.html)- serializer
- Entity serialization traits.
- [entity_](https://docs.rs/entity_store/index.html)- store
- Entity store for managing databases of typed entities.
- [error](https://docs.rs/error/index.html)
- Error types for the persistence layer.
- [evolve](https://docs.rs/evolve/index.html)
- Schema evolution support for the persistence layer.
- [primary_](https://docs.rs/primary_index/index.html)- index
- Primary index for typed entity access.
- [secondary_](https://docs.rs/secondary_index/index.html)- index
- Secondary index for typed entity access by a non-primary key.
- [secondary_](https://docs.rs/secondary_spec/index.html)- spec
- Compile-time metadata for secondary indexes declared via the
`#[derive(SecondaryKey)]`proc-macro.
- [sequence](https://docs.rs/sequence/index.html)
- Auto-incrementing sequences for entity ID generation.
- [simple_](https://docs.rs/simple_serializer/index.html)- serializer
- Simple binary serializer for entity persistence.
- [store_](https://docs.rs/store_config/index.html)- config
- Entity store configuration.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Catalog](https://docs.rs/struct.CatalogEntry.html)- Entry
- One row in the persistent catalog database.
- [Class](https://docs.rs/struct.ClassCatalog.html)- Catalog
- Wraps a hidden database and exposes the typed catalog operations.
- [Class](https://docs.rs/struct.ClassMutations.html)- Mutations
- The set of class-level mutations that apply to a specific class version.
- [Converter](https://docs.rs/struct.Converter.html)
- A mutation for converting an old version of an entity or field value to conform to the current class definition.
- [Decoded](https://docs.rs/struct.DecodedRecord.html)- Record
- A decoded envelope returned by `decode`
- [Deleter](https://docs.rs/struct.Deleter.html)
- A mutation that marks an entity class or field as deleted.
- [Entity](https://docs.rs/struct.EntityIterator.html)- Iterator
- Iterator over entities using a database cursor.
- [Entity](https://docs.rs/struct.EntityStore.html)- Store
- An entity store that manages databases for entity classes.
- [Evolve](https://docs.rs/struct.EvolveConfig.html)- Config
- Configuration for eager entity evolution.
- [Evolve](https://docs.rs/struct.EvolveStats.html)- Stats
- Statistics accumulated during eager entity evolution.
- [Field](https://docs.rs/struct.FieldDecoder.html)- Decoder
- A sequential field decoder that reads typed values from a byte buffer.
- [Field](https://docs.rs/struct.FieldEncoder.html)- Encoder
- A sequential field encoder that appends typed values to a byte buffer.
- [KeyIterator](https://docs.rs/struct.KeyIterator.html)
- Iterator over primary keys using a database cursor.
- [Memory](https://docs.rs/struct.MemorySequence.html)- Sequence
- An in-memory-only sequence that does not persist to a database.
- [Mutation](https://docs.rs/struct.MutationKey.html)- Key
- A key identifying a mutation target: (class_name, class_version, field_name).
- [Mutations](https://docs.rs/struct.Mutations.html)
- A collection of `Renamer``Deleter``Converter`
- [Primary](https://docs.rs/struct.PrimaryIndex.html)- Index

# noxu::xa - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/noxu/7.2.1/noxu/xa/index.html

## Expand description

XA distributed transactions (X/Open XA two-phase commit).

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [environment](https://docs.rs/environment/index.html)
- XA Environment — wraps a Noxu Environment to provide XA resource management.
- [error](https://docs.rs/error/index.html)
- XA error types.
- [flags](https://docs.rs/flags/index.html)
- XA flags and return codes.
- [prepared_](https://docs.rs/prepared_log/index.html)- log
- Persistent prepared-transaction log for XA crash recovery.
- [resource](https://docs.rs/resource/index.html)
- XA Resource Manager trait.
- [xid](https://docs.rs/xid/index.html)
- XA Transaction Identifier (Xid).

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Prepared](https://docs.rs/struct.PreparedLog.html)- Log
- Persistent log of prepared XA branches.
- [XaEnvironment](https://docs.rs/struct.XaEnvironment.html)
- XA-enabled wrapper around a Noxu Environment.
- [XaFlags](https://docs.rs/struct.XaFlags.html)
- XA flags passed to XA operations.
- [Xid](https://docs.rs/struct.Xid.html)
- XA Transaction Identifier.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Prepare](https://docs.rs/enum.PrepareResult.html)- Result
- Return value indicating the branch was read-only (no commit needed).
- [XaError](https://docs.rs/enum.XaError.html)
- XA errors returned from XaResource operations.
- [XidError](https://docs.rs/enum.XidError.html)
- Errors related to Xid construction.
